newsitem.title: UK: BAe acts to calm French fears on Airbus - paper.
newsitem.headline: BAe acts to calm French fears on Airbus - paper.

text.p: British Aerospace has reassured France it would not lose its aircraft factories and research establishments in the restructuring of Airbus Industrie, the Financial Times said on Wednesday.

It said BAe was seeking to allay the concerns of Airbus partner Aerospatiale that turning the aircraft manufacturing cooperative into a corporation would mean the French state firm giving up its core assets.

The newspaper quoted BAe managing director John Weston as saying in a speech prepared for a conference in Hanover that the incorporation of Airbus should be the precursor for a single European aerospace and defence company.
But the consolidation, which BAe and German Airbus partner Daimler-Benz unit Daimler Aerospace (DASA) have been calling for, would retain national identities, he was quoted as saying.
"The (new) company will need to retain national governments as customers and providers of investment in research and development," he said.

"Governments will rightly expect a return on such investment in terms of employment, the technological base and perhaps return from export sales. The new company will therefore need to seek an equitable but also industrially rational distribution of activities between the companies."
The four partners in Airbus agreed earlier this year to turn the consortium into a single company to make it more efficient and therefore more competitive against arch-rival Boeing Co .
They now want to decide by the end of this year what assets from each of the partners should be taken over by the new entity.
The other shareholder in Airbus is Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa).
